title: Best Asian Airlines for Families 2026
excerpt: Flying with kids in Asia? We've ranked the best Asian airlines for families in 2026 based on seat comfort, kids' meals, entertainment, stroller policies, and value. From Singapore Airlines to budget carriers, here's who makes your journey easiest.
author: Family Travel Asia Team
content:
Flying with kids in Asia can be a joy or a nightmare — and the airline you choose makes all the difference. In 2026, Asian carriers continue to dominate global airline rankings, and many of them go above and beyond for families. From Singapore Airlines' legendary service to budget airlines that surprise with their kid-friendliness, here's our definitive ranking of the best Asian airlines for families.

We've evaluated each airline on: seat comfort and legroom, kids' meal quality, entertainment options, stroller policy (gate check vs check-in), pre-boarding for families, and value for money.

## 1. Singapore Airlines

**🏆 Best Overall for Families**

Singapore Airlines is our top pick for families in 2026. It consistently ranks as one of the world's best airlines (Skytrax 5-star, World's Best Airline 2023) and offers exceptional service for families.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** Extensive menu including Halal, vegetarian, and allergy-friendly options. Book 24+ hours before. Kids get activity packs with crayons, puzzles, and stickers.
- **Entertainment:** KrisWorld system has 1,800+ options including dedicated kids' section with Disney+ content, movies, games, and music. 11.1-inch touchscreens even in economy.
- **Seating:** Economy seats have 32–34 inch pitch with adjustable headrests. Premium economy (38 inch pitch) is worth the upgrade for families.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed. Strollers returned at aircraft door upon arrival. No size limits on most routes.
- **Pre-boarding:** Families with children under 2 board first (Group 1).

**Typical fares:** Regional (e.g., Hong Kong–Singapore): $120–250 one way. Long-haul economy (e.g., London–Singapore): $600–900 one way.

**Best for:** Families who value service, food quality, and comfort above all.

## 2. ANA (All Nippon Airways)

**🏆 Best for Long-Haul with Toddlers**

Japan's 5-star carrier is a close second, especially for long-haul flights from North America and Europe to Asia.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** Japanese and Western options, beautifully presented in bento boxes. Baby food (pureed) available on request.
- **Entertainment:** On-demand video with 100+ movies, kids' channel, and Nintendo Switch games on select aircraft.
- **Seating:** Economy seats offer 33–34 inch pitch (generous by industry standards). Premium economy offers 38 inches.
- **Changing tables:** Available in almost all lavatories on wide-body aircraft — a rare and appreciated feature.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed. ANA provides plastic bags to protect strollers.
- **Child-free zone?** No, but ANA's quiet cabin policy means families are seated together in less disruptive areas.

**Typical fares:** Tokyo–Bangkok: $200–350 one way. Los Angeles–Tokyo: $700–1,200 one way.

**Best for:** Long-haul flights from the US/Europe to Japan and Asia.

## 3. Cathay Pacific

**🏆 Best for Comfort + Value**

Hong Kong's flagship carrier, ranked #1 in the 2026 AirlineRatings.com rankings, delivers a consistently excellent family experience.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** Dedicated children's menu with popular choices like pasta, chicken nuggets, and fruit. Baby meals (pureed) available.
- **Entertainment:** StudioCX features 1,000+ options with a dedicated kids' hub. Seat-back screens with HDMI/USB ports for personal devices.
- **Seating:** Economy has 31–32 inch pitch — slightly tighter than Singapore Airlines, but seats are well-padded with ergonomic design.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed on most routes. Strollers returned at the aircraft door.
- **Kids' amenities:** Activity packs for children 2–11 with coloring books, puzzles, and postcards.
- **Unaccompanied minor service:** Excellent for older kids flying solo — responsible and thorough.

**Typical fares:** Hong Kong–Tokyo: $150–300 one way. Hong Kong–London: $500–900 one way.

**Best for:** Families based in or transiting through Hong Kong.

## 4. EVA Air

**🏆 Best Hello Kitty Experience (Seriously!)**

Taiwan's 5-star airline offers a unique themed flying experience that kids absolutely adore.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Hello Kitty themed flights:** On select routes (Taipei–Tokyo, Taipei–Los Angeles, etc.), everything from the boarding music to the amenity kits to the meal napkins is Hello Kitty. It's a dream for young kids.
- **Kids' meals:** Excellent bento-style boxes with cute animal shapes and child-friendly portions.
- **Seating:** Economy seats are 32–33 inch pitch. Premium Laurel (premium economy) at 38 inches is excellent value.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed. EVA provides protective plastic bags.
- **Entertainment:** EVA's system has a dedicated kids' channel with cartoons, movies, and games.

**Typical fares:** Taipei–Tokyo: $150–280 one way. Taipei–Los Angeles: $600–1,000 one way.

**Best for:** Families with Hello Kitty–obsessed kids. The theme alone makes the flight memorable.

## 5. Japan Airlines (JAL)

**🏆 Best for Superb Service**

JAL is ANA's main rival and equally excellent for families.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** JAL's "Sky Kids" meal program offers Japanese and Western options. Book at least 24 hours before.
- **Lap children:** JAL allows infants under 2 to sit on a parent's lap. Bassinet seats available on long-haul flights (request at booking).
- **Entertainment:** MAGIC system with 100+ movies, TV shows, music, and games. Nintendo Switch available on some routes.
- **Seating:** Economy 33–34 inch pitch. Legroom is among the best in Asia.
- **Strollers:** Gate-check allowed. JAL also offers complimentary baby stroller rental at Tokyo Narita/Haneda airports!
- **Children flying alone:** JAL's "JAL Junior Pilot" program for ages 5–17 is thorough and well-reviewed.

**Typical fares:** Tokyo–Bangkok: $200–400 one way. Tokyo–New York: $800–1,200 one way.

**Best for:** Families flying to/from Japan with excellent service standards.

## 6. Bangkok Airways (Best Budget-Comfort Hybrid)

**🏆 Best Boutique Carrier**

Bangkok Airways brands itself as "Asia's Boutique Airline" and punches well above its weight for families.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Lounge access:** Even economy class passengers get access to Bangkok Airways lounges — and they have dedicated kids' corners with toys, games, and snacks.
- **Kids' meals:** Available on request, simple but good quality.
- **Seating:** Economy seats have 34 inch pitch — better than many full-service carriers.
- **Entertainment:** Personal screens on Airbus A320s. Free movies and games.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed.
- **Destinations:** Perfect for island-hopping families (Bangkok–Samui, Bangkok–Phuket, etc.).

**Typical fares:** Bangkok–Samui: $80–150 one way. Bangkok–Phnom Penh: $60–120 one way.

**Best for:** Families island-hopping in Thailand and Southeast Asia.

## 7. AirAsia (Best Budget Option)

**🏆 Best Value for Money**

Yes, a budget airline makes our list. AirAsia, Southeast Asia's largest low-cost carrier, understands families need to fly too.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Hot seats:** Pay a small fee ($5–15) to reserve exit row or front row seats with extra legroom. Worth every cent.
- **Quiet zone:** Selected flights have a quiet zone (rows 7–14) where children under 12 aren't allowed — handy if you're flying without kids. But if you're WITH kids, avoid booking these rows.
- **Meals:** Pre-book "Santan" meals for $4–6. Kids' meals available.
- **Booking:** Kids (2–11) and infants (under 2) discounted fares.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed. No charge for strollers.
- **Frequent sales:** Regular 0-fare seat sales make flying incredibly cheap.

**What to watch:** No seat-back entertainment (bring your own tablet). No pre-boarding for families. Seats don't recline. But you're paying $20–60 for a 2-hour flight — the value is undeniable.

**Typical fares:** Bangkok–Kuala Lumpur: $25–60 one way. Kuala Lumpur–Singapore: $15–40 one way.

**Best for:** Budget-conscious families flying short-to-medium haul routes.

## 8. Vietnam Airlines

**🏆 Best for Vietnam Travel**

Vietnam's national carrier has improved significantly and offers great value for families exploring Vietnam.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** Available on international routes. Simple but kid-friendly options.
- **Entertainment:** AVOD system on international flights with movies, games, and music. Domestic flights may have overhead screens only.
- **Seating:** Economy 32–33 inch pitch. Premium Economy on A350 and B787 offers 38 inches.
- **Lotus Lounge:** Access with premium tickets. Basic but quiet.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed.

**Typical fares:** Hanoi–Ho Chi Minh City: $40–80 one way. Ho Chi Minh City–Bangkok: $60–120 one way.

**Best for:** Families traveling within Vietnam or connecting to Indochina.

## 9. Thai Airways

**🏆 Best Royal Orchid Service**

Thailand's flagship carrier offers warm, gracious service that extends beautifully to families.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Kids' meals:** Available on advance order. Thai and Western options. Good portion sizes.
- **Entertainment:** Dedicated kids' channel with cartoons and Disney movies. Kids get activity kits on long-haul.
- **Seating:** Economy 32–34 inch pitch. Royal Silk (business) is very family-friendly.
- **Bangkok lounge:** Royal Orchid Spa (free foot/neck massage) can save worn-out parents.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed.
- **Routes:** Excellent connections across Asia, Europe, Australia.

**Typical fares:** Bangkok–Tokyo: $200–400 one way. Bangkok–London: $500–900 one way.

**Best for:** Families connecting through Bangkok with warm Thai hospitality.

## 10. Cebu Pacific (Best Philippine Budget Option)

**🏆 Best for Philippines Island Hopping**

Cebu Pacific is the leading low-cost carrier in the Philippines and a great option for families traveling between islands.

**Family-friendly features:**
- **Cebu Pacific Fun Games:** In-flight trivia and games on selected flights keep kids engaged.
- **Stroller policy:** Gate-check allowed, free of charge.
- **Seat selection:** Choose your seats at booking (small fee). Pick front rows for easier access.
- **Infant fees:** Infants under 2 pay only 10% of adult fare (plus taxes).
- **Meals:** Pre-book "Yummy Picks" meals for $4–6. Kids' meal options available.

**Typical fares:** Manila–Cebu: $25–60 one way. Manila–Hong Kong: $40–100 one way.

**Best for:** Budget families exploring the Philippines.

## Pro Tips for Flying with Kids in Asia

1. **Book early morning flights.** Kids are fresher in the morning, and delays compound less.
2. **Pre-order kids' meals** 24–48 hours in advance on full-service carriers.
3. **Gate check your stroller** — never check it with luggage. You need it in the terminal.
4. **Pack snacks for budget airlines.** AirAsia, Cebu Pacific, and other LCCs charge for food. Bring your own.
5. **Download entertainment** before flying on budget airlines (no screens = bring a tablet with pre-downloaded shows).
6. **Seat selection:** On all carriers, pay for exit row or front row seats for extra legroom with a lap child bassinet option.
7. **Baby bassinets** are available on long-haul flights (Singapore Airlines, ANA, Cathay, JAL, Thai, EVA) — request at booking, as only 4–8 are available per plane.
8. **Airport lounges:** If you have lounge access (priority pass, credit card, etc.), use them. Many Asian lounges have kids' rooms.

Flying with kids in Asia doesn't have to be stressful. The region's airlines are world-class and genuinely cater to families. Choose based on your route, budget, and what matters most to you — and you'll arrive at your destination with your sanity intact.
